premises.text: Consumers can remotely top up and manage a contactless transit card from phone/cloud wherever they are
premises.evidence_span: They can top up their card while on their way to the bus, while waiting for the bus from the hotel room or even from their home city, wherever and whenever they are

premises.text: The Fidesmo card integrates into operators' existing ticketing infrastructure so phones become sales channels without new physical infrastructure
premises.evidence_span: the Videsmo card integrates seamlessly into their existing infrastructure

premises.text: MIFARE-based contactless standards cover most global ticketing systems, enabling multi-city one-card use
premises.evidence_span: 70% of all contactless ticketing systems in the world are based on MyFair, and we intend to take advantage of that

premises.text: Distribution and monetization run through public-transport operators with a percentage take on ticket sales
premises.evidence_span: we intend to sell a lot of tickets and take a percentage on those

premises.text: An open API platform lets third parties add loyalty, hotel-key, and secure-access services on the same card
premises.evidence_span: Fidesmo is, at the core, an API. We invite other companies to build services on top of our platform

value.text: One connected card that simplifies multi-city transit and related services via cloud management
value.evidence_span: We will make one card to replace them all

causal_links.evidence_span: it's easy to use, and it gives them control
every phone becomes a sales channel
we want everyone to use our card or card space on our platform

notes: Transcript opens mid-pitch (IP/workflow mention truncated). ASR MyFair/Videsmo corrected in premise text; evidence spans verbatim. Market-size and Oyster-card counts treated as sizing/traction. Future phone embedding treated as aspiration. Singletons D2/D3 retained as independently revisable monetization and platform-extension modules.
